tools.name: port_day_guide
tools.description: Plan one time-boxed day in an unfamiliar port city — typically a cruise port day, or any stop with a fixed arrival and departure time. Given the port and the ship's local arrival and departure times, returns: the usable time ashore (after disembarking, keeping a safe return margin before all-aboard)

tools.name: start_cruise_plan
tools.description: For a traveler who has already chosen a specific cruise (ship + departure date) and wants the whole trip planned around it: flights, hotels before and after the cruise, and every port day. Checks whether Cruise Planner knows this sailing and returns a link to the planner where the traveler continues

tools.name: plan_cruise_connections
tools.description: Plan how to get to and from a cruise. Given the embarkation and disembarkation ports and dates, returns for each port the gateway airport (IATA code and distance), the recommended arrival date (the day before embarkation) and the same-day arrival rule, the earliest safe flight time on disembarkation

tools.name: get_plan_status
tools.description: Check a Cruise Planner trip plan that the traveler shared with you. Input the share token or the full share link (…/trip/s/<token>). Returns which stages are filled (cruise, brief, flights, hotels, port days), whether the plan is complete, and links to the shared plan and its PDF. Plans of signed-in

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: start_cruise_plan · Private data: start_cruise_plan, get_plan_status · Public sink: get_plan_status.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: start_cruise_plan · Private data: start_cruise_plan, get_plan_status · Public sink: get_plan_status

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
